title: छिमेकी कथामा यथार्थवाद {Realism in neighborhood fiction}
nepali: यस अध्ययनमा नेपाली कथा परम्परामा आधुनिकता भित्र्याउने कथाकार गुरुप्रसाद मैनालीको ‘नासो’ कथासङ्ग्रहमा सङ्ग्रहित ‘छिमेकी’ कथामा यथार्थवादको प्रयोगलाई विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यसमा पुस्तकालयीय कार्यबाट सामग्री सङ्कलन गरी गुणात्मक अनुसन्धान ढाँचामा व्याख्या र विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । कथामाकरेसा जोडिएका छिमेकी आफन्त भन्दा पनि नजिकको सम्बन्धमा रहेका हुन्छन् र सानातिना समस्यालाईवास्ता नगरी एकलाई पर्दा अर्काको सहयोग गर्नुको विकल्प नहुने विचार प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । ग्रामीण जनजीवनका यथार्थ घटनामा आधारित रहेको हुँदा पूर्वीय तथा पाश्चात्य यथार्थवादको मान्यताका आधारमा प्रस्तुत कथा यथार्थवादी भएको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । {In this study, the use of realism in the 'Chhimeki' story collected in the 'Naso' story collection of the storyteller Guru Prasad Mainali, who brought modernity into the Nepali story tradition, is analyzed. In this, materials from library work have been collected and interpreted and analyzed in a qualitative research format. As it is based on the real events of rural people's life, it has been concluded that the story presented is realistic based on the beliefs of Eastern and Western realism.}
american_english: In this study, the use of realism in the story 'Chhimeki' ('The Neighbor'), collected in the short story anthology 'Naso' by fiction writer Guru Prasad Mainali, who ushered modernity into the Nepali short story tradition, is analyzed. In this research, materials were collected through library work and interpreted and analyzed within a qualitative research framework. In the story, next-door neighbors sharing adjacent backyards are situated in a relationship even closer than relatives, and the idea is presented that, disregarding minor problems, there is no alternative to helping one another when someone faces hardship. Being based on the real events of rural life, it is concluded that, on the basis of the tenets of Eastern and Western realism, the presented story is realistic.
british_english: In this study, the application of realism in the story 'Chhimeki' ('The Neighbour'), collected in the short story anthology 'Naso' by fiction writer Guru Prasad Mainali, who ushered modernity into the Nepali short-story tradition, is analysed. In this research, materials have been collected through library work and interpreted and analysed within a qualitative research framework. In the story, next-door neighbours whose backyards adjoin are in a relationship even closer than relatives, and the idea is put forward that, disregarding minor problems, there is no alternative to helping one another when someone faces hardship. Grounded as it is in the real events of rural life, it is concluded that, on the basis of the conventions of Eastern and Western realism, the presented story is realistic.

In this research, materials were collected through library work and interpreted and analysed within a qualitative research framework. In the story, next-door neighbours whose backyards join up are situated in a relationship even closer than relatives, and the idea is presented that, disregarding minor problems, there is no alternative to helping one another when someone faces hardship. informal_english: In this study, the use of realism in the yarn 'Chhimeki' ('The Neighbour'), collected in the short story collection 'Naso' by story writer Guru Prasad Mainali—the bloke who brought modernity into the Nepali short story tradition—gets analysed. For this one, materials were gathered through library work, then unpacked and analysed within a qualitative research framework. In the story, neighbours with adjoining backyards are in a bond even closer than relatives, and the idea is put across that, without worrying about petty squabbles, there's no way around lending a hand when a mate runs into trouble. Since it's based on real-life happenings in rural life, the conclusion is reached that, on the basis of both Eastern and Western realism, the presented story is fair dinkum realistic.
